title: Boat and Helicopter Tourism
desc: Plan a small boat or helicopter tour offering with safe operations, licences, weather rules, guest care and pricing.
outcomes: Explain operator duties and passenger safety.
Compute cost per hour and per guest.
task: Plan a tour product with route, safety briefing, weather rules, licences, price and incident plan, working with licensed operators.
condition: A computer, a map, a spreadsheet, two peers and a licensed operator mentor. Learners do not operate vessels or aircraft.
standard: Licences and insurance are checked with sources; weather go/no-go rules are written; briefing covers equipment and emergencies; cost per guest is correct; peers rate Meets or better.
who: Tour planners, guides, hotel desks, port staff.
evidence: route plan, briefing script, go/no-go rules, price sheet

quiz: Who may operate?
Licensed operators and crew. (Covered in module 1: Product and route. To pass that module: Map and timings.)
Go/no-go factors?
Wind, visibility, waves or ceiling. (Covered in module 2: Licences and insurance. To pass that module: Sources and dates.)
Briefing items?
Equipment, exits, behaviour. (Covered in module 3: Weather and go/no-go. To pass that module: Numbers specified.)
Cost per guest?
Hourly cost x hours / guests. (Covered in module 4: Briefing and equipment. To pass that module: Under five minutes.)
Why drills?
Find weaknesses. (Covered in module 5: Emergencies. To pass that module: Steps ordered.)
Insurance for?
Passengers. (Covered in module 6: Cost and pricing. To pass that module: Currency shown.)
Why check expiry?
Valid permits. (Covered in module 7: Environment and community. To pass that module: Controls clear.)
Environment control?
Avoid nesting sites. (Covered in module 8: Operations plan. To pass that module: Complete.)
Cancel policy?
Refund. (Covered in module 8: Operations plan. To pass that module: Complete.)
What are checks logged?
Equipment inspection. (Covered in module 8: Operations plan. To pass that module: Complete.)

ladder: Product and route

L1: learner can name tour types. Focus module: Product and route (Understand, 3 h). Design a tour that guests will value and operators can run safely. Key points: Types: scenic, sunset, wildlife, transfer. Duration, capacity, ports and landing sites. Accessibility and comfort. Seasonality. Add a weather back-up day and an indoor alternative.

Teach: open with the worked example. A 45-minute coastal route with a sunset slot and a 20-minute boarding window. A rainy-day harbour museum visit replaces the cruise. Then set the activity: Design a route with times. Add a backup plan. Mark against the standard: Map and timings. Check at this level: Who may operate? Model answer: Licensed operators and crew.
Licences and insurance

L2: learner knows licence basics. Focus module: Licences and insurance (Apply, 5 h). Only licensed operators and crews run commercial trips. Key points: Vessel or aircraft certificates, crew licences and operator permits. Insurance for passengers. Check expiry dates. Keep copies. Verify operator documents with the authority where possible.

Teach: open with the worked example. A certificate expires next month; bookings after that date are stopped until renewal. A tour desk asks for an up-to-date certificate before each season. Then set the activity: Make a checklist. Add a seasonal check. Mark against the standard: Sources and dates. Check at this level: Go/no-go factors? Model answer: Wind, visibility, waves or ceiling.
Weather and go/no-go

L3: learner can read weather rules. Focus module: Weather and go/no-go (Apply, 5 h). Safety over schedule. Key points: Wind, visibility, waves and ceiling. Clear numbers and a named decision maker. Refund policy for cancellations. Record decisions. Use two independent weather sources.

Teach: open with the worked example. Wind above a set limit cancels flights and guests are offered a new date or refund. Two forecasts disagree; the cautious one is followed. Then set the activity: Write rules. Name your sources. Mark against the standard: Numbers specified. Check at this level: Briefing items? Model answer: Equipment, exits, behaviour.
Briefing and equipment

L4: learner can brief guests. Focus module: Briefing and equipment (Apply, 4 h). Guests must know what to do. Key points: Life jackets, seat belts, exits and behaviour. Language options and check understanding. Equipment inspection log. Accessibility. Give briefing in the guest language or with pictures.

Teach: open with the worked example. Guests repeat how to fasten a life jacket before boarding. A picture card shows life-jacket fastening. Then set the activity: Write a briefing script. Create a picture card. Mark against the standard: Under five minutes. Check at this level: Cost per guest? Model answer: Hourly cost x hours / guests.
Emergencies

L5: learner can price. Focus module: Emergencies (Evaluate, 4 h). Plan and drill. Key points: Man overboard, fire, engine failure and medical. Contacts and roles. Practice drills. Review after drills. Practice a man-overboard drill every month.

Teach: open with the worked example. A drill finds the radio channel was wrong and the sheet is corrected. The crew recovers a dummy in 90 seconds. Then set the activity: Write a plan. Record drill times. Mark against the standard: Steps ordered. Check at this level: Why drills? Model answer: Find weaknesses.
Environment and community

L6: learner can lead. Focus module: Environment and community (Evaluate, 3 h). Be a good neighbour. Key points: Noise, wildlife and emissions. Flight paths and speed rules. Local jobs. Respect for residents. Publish noise and altitude commitments.

Teach: open with the worked example. Routes avoid nesting sites in season. Operators fly above 300 m over residential areas. Then set the activity: List controls. Add commitments. Mark against the standard: Controls clear. Check at this level: Insurance for? Model answer: Passengers.
Operations plan

L7: learner can audit. Focus module: Operations plan (Create, 3 h). Write and present. Key points: Roles, schedule and records. Review each season. Guest feedback. Training. Prepare a complaint and refund process.

Teach: open with the worked example. The plan reaches 4.7 average guest score. Refunds within 7 days after cancellation. Then set the activity: Present. Add a refund rule. Mark against the standard: Complete. Check at this level: Why check expiry? Model answer: Valid permits.
